13.text: THEFT. — As I have stated before, thefts frequently occur among the

14.text: Chukchee, especially among the reindeer-breeders. The chief objects taken

23.text: Thus the result depends much on the strength and the temper of the con-

24.text: testing parties. I will mention a few such cases within my knowledge.

25.text: One reindeer-breeder, a man of peaceful temper, lost a group of reindeer,

26.text: nine in number, which strayed away from the herd, as reindeer often do, and

27.text: could not be found. It appeared afterwards that they had gone to the herd

28.text: of one of the neighboring camps, and had been appropriated by the master.

29.text: His own camp assistant gave information of the fact; but the offender was

30.text: obstinate, and denied it till the end. Then the wronged man became angry,

31.text: and sent his people to seek retribution. His son and one of his neighbors

32.text: visited the herd of the offender in the latter’s absence, and took from it two

33.text: strong driving-reindeer, one young buck well broken, and three reindeer of

34.text: the average sort. They said to the herdsmen, “Go and tell the master that
